benefits: Peek inside a ZIP before downloading or extracting it.
See real uncompressed sizes to check you have disk space.
Spot encrypted files and odd compression methods instantly.
No upload — your archive never leaves your device.

faqs.a: This tool only reads the ZIP's central directory — the index at the end of the file that lists every entry. It does not decompress anything, which is why listing is instant even for large archives.

Compression ratio = (1 − packed size ÷ original size) × 100. Text files often compress 60–80%; already-compressed formats like JPEG, MP4, and PNG barely shrink, so a low ratio on those is normal, not a problem.
faqs.q: What does the compression ratio mean?

faqs.a: The padlock badge marks entries with the encryption flag set. This viewer cannot read encrypted contents, and the companion ZIP File Extractor will skip them too — that is a deliberate safety boundary, not a bug.
faqs.q: What does the padlock badge mean?

faqs.a: Yes. The central directory stores each entry's original size, packed size, compression method, and name — everything this tool shows. Filenames are decoded as UTF-8, which covers virtually all modern archives.
faqs.q: Can it list any ZIP file?

faqs.a: Multi-disk (spanned) archives and ZIP64 files larger than 4 GB are not supported — the tool shows a parse error for those. Standard single-file ZIPs from Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android all work.
faqs.q: Are there ZIP types it cannot read?

faqs.a: The 200 MB cap keeps the browser tab responsive. The whole archive is read into memory to parse the index, and very large files can freeze low-memory phones. For bigger archives, use desktop software.
faqs.q: Why is there a 200 MB file limit?

zip-archive-content-viewer.formula:
Listing is index reading, not arithmetic.
Compression ratio = (1 − packed ÷ original) × 100
Parsed from the ZIP central directory (signature 0x02014b50 entries at the end-of-central-directory offset).
howTo: Click Choose file and pick a .zip from your device.
The archive index is read instantly in your browser.
Browse the file list: names, sizes, methods, and ratios.

keyFacts: A ZIP file ends with a central directory — an index of every entry.
Each entry stores its name, sizes, method, and encryption flag.
Stored = no compression; Deflated = standard ZIP compression.
The viewer reads the index only; nothing is decompressed.
Encrypted entries are flagged but their contents stay hidden.
Files up to 200 MB are accepted.

It reads only the archive's index, so even large ZIPs list in a blink. Nothing is uploaded; the file never leaves your device.

zip-archive-content-viewer.workedExample:
A ZIP with report.pdf (1,000,000 bytes → 620,000 packed) and notes.txt (50,000 → 12,000 packed):
1. report.pdf ratio = (1 − 620,000/1,000,000) × 100 = 38% saved.
2. notes.txt ratio = (1 − 12,000/50,000) × 100 = 76% saved.
3. Totals: 2 files, 1,050,000 B original, 632,000 B packed, 39.8% saved overall.
